key_insight: Friction stir welding joined dissimilar AISI 316L and AISI 444 stainless steels with strong grain refinement, high cohesion, and no observed defects or undesirable phases.
engineering_relevance: The process offers a promising route for joining austenitic and ferritic stainless steels while limiting adverse microstructural changes.
method: Compared one butt-joint and two overlap-joint configurations.
Applied axial forces of 25–50 kN and rotation speeds of 350–450 rpm at a constant welding speed of 1 mm/s.
Examined microstructural evolution across base metal, heat-affected, thermomechanically affected, and stir zones.
evidence_signal: Across the tested conditions, no relevant base-metal-to-heat-affected-zone changes or chi, sigma, and Laves phases were observed; placing AISI 316L on top in overlap joints reduced upper-to-lower differences in grain deformation and recrystallisation.
watch_item: The abstract reports microstructural observations but does not quantify joint strength, fatigue life, or corrosion performance.
paper_title: Microstructure Evolution of Dissimilar AISI 316L and AISI 444 Stainless Steel Joints by Friction Stir Welding
